title: Geometry and Constants in Finite Relativistic Algebra
content: We show that a single finite field, built from any odd prime \(p\), already contains everything needed to mimic smooth geometry and Fourier analysis. By arranging the field’s basic arithmetic moves in a 4-dimensional symmetry cube, we obtain a finite lattice that has the same combinatorial shape as a 2-sphere. Completing the field with infinitesimals turns this lattice into a genuinely smooth surface with constant curvature. The field itself also provides finite versions of the familiar constants \(i, \pi\) and \(e\), identified by their structural roles. Using these constants we build a Fourier kernel that works simultaneously in the finite and continuous settings, merging the usual and the discrete Fourier transforms into one framework. In short, smooth geometry, fundamental mathematical constants, and harmonic analysis can all arise from finite arithmetic alone.
